column1: # Persian verb stems: infinitive, past stem(s), present stem(s); alternates split by "|".
# Where a present stem changes after ب، ن or می (pp. 38–39 of the Academy's دستور خط
# فارسی), the written alternate is listed too: آمدن has آ and یا.
# Sources: the standard grammars' paradigm tables; John Mace, Persian Grammar: For
#   Reference and Revision, Appendix I, pp. 209–211 (his transliteration separates
#   raftan/rav- 'go' from roftan/rub- 'sweep'); and class rules, each with its
#   exceptions named: ـیدن drops یدن, ـاندن drops دن, ـودن → ـا, ـاختن ـیختن ـوختن → ـز,
# Every stem was checked against a 3.98M-segment Persian corpus for finite present
#   forms its own past stem cannot produce (می‌دید is not evidence for a stem دی).
#   Rarity did not disqualify; ambiguity did.
# Declined: آر for آوردن (bare آرد is the noun 'flour'); preverb compounds
#   (verb-preverbs.tsv); بایدن، درایدن، زدیدن، گرودن (not verbs); مزیدن، سربریدن،
#   باشیدن (their evidence belongs to other words).
